findings: Buys: over the five trading days from the fill, the stocks it bought beat SPY by 0.07% on average (41 buys, 56% of them ahead of SPY; t = 0.1, within noise).
Sells: over the five trading days from the fill, the stocks it sold beat SPY by 1.11%, so selling gave that up (52 sells; t = -1.5, within noise).
Decision IC: on the 19 days it traded, what it bought ranked against what it sold and left alone by a mean rank IC of -0.023 with the next five days' returns (IC IR -0.14, t = -0.6, within noise).
Holdings IC: the weights it held after each of 43 decision days had a mean rank IC of 0.004 with the next five days' returns (t = 0.3, within noise).
Factor exposures: market 0.70 (t 17.6), size 0.03 (t 0.6), growth -0.56 (t -10.8), momentum 0.04 (t 1.8); together they explain 67% of the daily variation (R²).
Of its +9.5% a year over T-bills (arithmetic mean): market +7.5%, growth -1.4%, momentum -1.0%, size +0.1%; the alpha left is +4.3% a year (t = 0.8, within noise).
Verdict: most of the return is factor exposure (+5.3% a year, market above all); the alpha left is not significant.
P&L: +$11,486 in all, +$10,607 from 12 positions and +$879 of interest on idle cash.
By holding period: 61+ days made the most (+$11,393, 11 positions); 21-60 days lost the most (-$786, 1 position).
By sector: Technology made the most (+$4,605, 4 positions); Communication Services lost the most (-$786, 1 position).
By stock: AAPL made the most (+$3,559, 1 position); NVDA lost the most (-$935, 1 position).
By market regime of the previous close: risk-on 96 days +0.5% (SPY +2.0%); neutral 18 days +2.0% (SPY +4.5%); uncertain 97 days +7.3% (SPY +4.8%); risk-off 6 days +1.3% (SPY +0.3%).
News: 1 positions opened on news made +$1,521, the other 11 +$9,087; over the five days from the fill, news-triggered buys trailed SPY by 0.67% (t -0.2).

Concentration: the profit rests on the best two positions, which made 57% of the positions' net P&L and 48% of all their gains; the best was AAPL bought 2026-01-12 and still open at the end, +$3,559. Had the best position made nothing, the run would have returned +7.9% instead of +11.5%.
